attempts.summary: Published node4's lan-b HTTP service (port 8080) on TCP port 80 of node2's (OPNsense) transit address 10.10.10.2 via a destination-NAT port-forward, and gave node1 (VyOS) a route to that transit address by assigning its transit interface (eth1=10.10.10.1/30) and lan-a interface (eth2=10.10.20.254/24). node3 on lan-a now reaches the service by curling node2's transit address only, with no direct route/reachability to node4. Discovered and fixed two non-obvious issues: (1) OPNsense pf evaluates filter 'pass' rules against the POST-NAT destination, so the pass rule had to target 10.10.30.10:8080 (not the original 10.10.10.2:80); (2) node2 needed an explicit static route back to lan-a (10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.1) since it is two hops away, not directly connected. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (node4, node2, node1, node3), with boot-identity change proven via boot_id/kern.boottime and uptime, and full recovery of addressing, NAT/firewall rules, static routes, the http-lanb systemd service, and end-to-end curl reachability confirmed after each restart.
